metaDesc: A 2-day, 1-night Prachinburi family itinerary in Thailand: Abhaibhubejhr herb garden, shallow Khao Ito waterfall, a dinosaur park and Chakraphong reservoir, with hours, fees and tips for traveling with kids.

ogTitle: Prachinburi With Kids: 2-Day Family Trip in Thailand
ogDesc: An easy family trip to Prachinburi: a shallow waterfall kids can splash in, a herb garden and a dinosaur park, just over an hour's drive from Bangkok.
intro: Prachinburi is one of the easiest places to take kids in Thailand. It's only a bit over an hour from Bangkok, the sights are clustered close together, and there's a mix of shallow waterfalls kids can splash in, a relaxed herb garden to stroll through, and a dinosaur park they'll love. We've laid out a 2-day, 1-night plan that isn't packed too tight, with time built in for kids to rest and take an afternoon nap.

blocks.html: If you want to get the kids out for some fresh air without a long drive, Prachinburi hits the sweet spot. For families, the standout is Khao Ito waterfall, where the water is shallow and gentle enough for kids to play in, and the nature spots and learning-focused sights all sit within a few kilometers of each other. This plan starts the morning at an easy pace, leaves time to rest in the afternoon, and avoids long walks for families with little ones.

blocks.text: Before You Go — When to Visit and How to Get There

blocks.html: The best time to bring kids for the waterfall is late rainy season into early cool season (September–December), when there's plenty of water but it isn't rushing. In the hot season the flow drops and some spots are left with just shallow pools. If you go during heavy rains, check the waterfall conditions first, since flash floods can come on fast.

items: From Bangkok — about 1.5–2 hours via the motorway / Route 304. The main sights are on the Khao Ito side of Mueang district.
Pack for the kids — a change of clothes, towels, grippy water shoes for walking on the slippery waterfall rocks, hats and insect repellent.
A private car is easiest — the sights are spread out beyond the town center and public transport barely reaches them, so driving yourself is the way to go with kids.

blocks.title: Tip for Little Kids
blocks.html: Start at the waterfall mid-morning before the sun gets harsh, then save the indoor stops, like the herb garden or a museum, for the afternoon when the kids start to flag. It helps keep the meltdowns away mid-trip.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Prachinburi trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Prachinburi
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Day 1 — Khao Ito Waterfall + Dinosaur Park

items.note: Grab breakfast and kids' snacks on the way; you'll reach Khao Ito around 10am.

items.activity: Khao Ito Waterfall, Khao Ito Recreation Forest, Ban Phra, Mueang district
items.note: A small, multi-tier waterfall; each pool is shallow with gentle flow, so kids can play. It's a short walk from the parking area. Open 08:00–16:30.

items.activity: Lunch at a restaurant by the waterfall
items.note: There are made-to-order spots and som tam by the water. Get the kids into dry clothes before they eat.
A large reservoir at the foot of the hills with nice views. Stroll along the dam, take photos, and there's a cycling area. Open roughly 08:30–17:30.
Plenty of big, hand-sculpted dinosaurs of different species that kids love. Free entry and fun for photos.
Pick a place in town or a resort at the foot of the hills, and let the kids shower and rest before dinner.
Restaurants in town serve made-to-order dishes, mookata (Thai BBQ hot pot) and boat noodles, all kid-friendly.

blocks.html: Day one focuses on outdoor activities while the kids still have energy. Khao Ito waterfall is where local families come to splash around on weekends because the water is shallow and it's close to the parking area. The dinosaur park is a bonus that nearly every kid enjoys, and it's free to enter.

blocks.title: About the Waterfall
blocks.html: In the dry season Khao Ito waterfall shrinks a lot, leaving just small pools. If you're set on plenty of water play, late rainy season into early cool season is the better bet. Keep an eye on the kids up close, since the waterfall rocks are slippery.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Learning in the Shade, Nothing Strenuous

items.note: Ease into the day. Most of today's activities are indoors with little walking.

items.activity: Abhaibhubejhr Herb Garden / Herbal Learning Center
items.note: Walk through the shady herb beds, let the kids smell the herbs and learn about the plants. There are pretty photo spots, and it's a comfortable, shaded stroll.

items.activity: Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Building (Thai Traditional Medicine Museum)
items.note: A handsome yellow European-style old building. Free entry, open 08:00–16:00, and great for family photos.
Around Abhaibhubejhr there are restaurants and health-focused cafes, with kid-friendly dishes too.

items.activity: Prachinburi National Museum (if the kids are still up for it)
items.note: Open Wed–Sun 09:00–16:00, 30 THB for Thai adults, free for students in uniform. Displays antiquities from eastern Thailand.
Popular Prachinburi souvenirs are Abhaibhubejhr herbal products and seasonal santol fruit.

blocks.html: Day two is designed to be lighter than the first, since kids are usually tired from the water play the day before. The activities are about strolling in the shade and indoors, with no long walks or sun. The herb garden and the Abhaibhubejhr building are in the same area, just a few minutes' drive apart, so you don't lose time getting between them.

blocks.text: Backup Spots If You Have Extra Time

items.name: Than Thip Waterfall, Bridge 2
items.blurb: In Prachantakham district, the draw here is that it's lit up at night so you can play in the water after dark, an unusual atmosphere. On weekends it stays open late, great if your family wants to try something different.

items.name: Takhro Waterfall
items.blurb: In Bu Fai subdistrict, Prachantakham. Genuinely natural, few people and very quiet, with no restaurants nearby. Good for families wanting to escape the crowds, but bring your own food and water.

items.name: Khao Ito Viewpoint & Campground
items.blurb: If your family likes camping, the Khao Ito area has a campground by the reservoir, with mountain views and cool, pleasant air in the morning.

items: Entry fees — Khao Ito waterfall, the dinosaur park and the Abhaibhubejhr building are all free. Your main costs are parking and food.
National Museum — 30 THB per Thai adult; students in uniform enter free.
Accommodation — resorts and hotels in town start from the high hundreds to low thousands of THB per night, depending on the season and room type.
Food for 2 days — eating at local spots runs roughly 600–1,000 THB per meal for a family of four.

blocks.title: Saving as a Family
blocks.html: Because many of the main sights are free, Prachinburi can be done on a modest budget. Go on a weekday and accommodation is usually cheaper and the sights less crowded, making it easier to walk around with kids than on a weekend.

faq.q: How many days is ideal for visiting Prachinburi with kids?
faq.a: Two days and one night is just right. Day one is the Khao Ito waterfall and dinosaur park, and day two is an easy stroll through the herb garden and the Abhaibhubejhr building. If you only have one day, you can stick to the Khao Ito area alone, since the sights are close together.

faq.q: Can kids swim at Khao Ito waterfall?
faq.a: Yes. Khao Ito is a small, multi-tier waterfall where each pool is shallow and the flow is gentle, so kids can play. The rocks are slippery, though, so supervise closely and have them wear water shoes. The water is fullest from late rainy season into early cool season.

Many of the main sights are free, including Khao Ito waterfall, the dinosaur park and the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr building. The Prachinburi National Museum charges 30 THB for Thai adults, with free entry for students in uniform.

faq.q: Which days are the Abhaibhubejhr building and museum open?
faq.a: The Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr building is open daily 08:00–16:00 with free entry. The Prachinburi National Museum is open Wed–Sun 09:00–16:00 and closed Monday–Tuesday. It's worth double-checking the hours before a long weekend.
Not far. It's about a 1.5–2 hour drive from Bangkok via the motorway / Route 304, making it a good fit for a family weekend trip when you don't want a long drive.
